summary_responses.response: The paper introduces DiffTry, a retry-based mechanism designed to protect high-priority transactions when independently managed microservices become overloaded. It assigns different retry limits to request classes, giving valuable requests more chances to succeed while restricting low-priority retries that can amplify overload or attacks. DiffTry is lightweight, distributed, and stateless, requiring neither overload detection nor coordination between services. The researchers develop mathematical models to predict rejection rates and throughput across individual services and entire networks, establishing convergence and prioritization guarantees under their assumptions. Simulations and a live Kubernetes deployment closely match the predictions, demonstrating that DiffTry can provide network-wide prioritization through a service-mesh plugin without application-code changes.

key_fact_breakdown.key_fact: DiffTry (Differential Retries) is a stateless mechanism that assigns different retry-attempt limits to different priority classes of requests to achieve differentiation in rejection rates.
Under overload with DiffTry, high-priority requests achieve a rejection rate of around 15% and account for about 85% of successful completions when both classes contribute 50% of input load.
DiffTry requires neither overload sensing nor microservices coordination and is implemented as a drop-in service-mesh plugin requiring no application code changes.

The paper develops an analytical model for DiffTry starting with two services in tandem, then generalizes it to networks of services using an open-network model combined with flow classes and priorities.

summary_responses.response: The Office of Personnel Management (OPM) has issued a direct final rule updating federal Family and Medical Leave Act (FMLA) regulations to reflect statutory changes enacted in 2021 and 2023. Virtually all federal civilian service, including past temporary or intermittent employment, and qualifying honorable active service in the Army, Navy, Air Force, Space Force, or Marine Corps count toward the 12-month service requirement for FMLA and paid parental leave eligibility. The rule also reflects that annual or sick leave earned under non-title 5 authorities may replace unpaid FMLA leave, although existing regulations already permit this substitution. Certain Veterans Health Administration employees are excluded from title 5 FMLA coverage and instead receive family and medical leave under separate Veterans Affairs law. The rule takes effect December 14, 2026, unless OPM receives significant adverse comments by November 16, 2026, in which case it will withdraw the affected provisions and initiate a proposed rulemaking.
